predecessors.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
predecessors.text: Egypt, taken when the Bahri Mamluks overthrew the Ayyubids in 1250

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Syria (after Marj Dabiq, 24 August 1516), Egypt (22 January 1517) and the Hejaz; Yemen only partly ('control of Yemen remained partial and sporadic')

ledger.x: 1250: the Bahri Mamluks overthrow the Ayyubids in Egypt and found the Mamluk sultanate.
1260: the Ayyubid princes of Hama (and Homs until 1262) keep their rule as Mamluk vassals.
1260: the Mamluks march north to meet the Mongols.
1260: the Mamluks take Damascus after Ain Jalut.

ledger.cp: Ayyubid emirate of Homs (al-Ashraf Musa; no dossier)

ledger.x: c. 1263: Kerak is surrendered to Baibars. 'al-Mughith Umar was tricked into surrendering Karak to Baibars', 'the next year' after al-Ashraf Musa's death in 1262. [Reviewer me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Counterpart changed from ayyubid-sultanate, whose dossier ends in 1260: the Ayyubid dynasty page, 'The next year, al-Mughith…
ledger.cp: Ayyubid emirate of Kerak (al-Mughith Umar; no dossier)

ledger.x: 1265: Baibars begins taking the Frankish coast.
1276: Lower Nubia is ceded, on paper.
1281: the Mongols are beaten back to the Euphrates.
1291: Acre falls and the Franks lose the mainland.
1291: the fighting for the Frankish coast ends.
1366: the Mamluks give up on Makuria.
1375: Sis falls and Cilician Armenia ends.
1382: the Burji Mamluks replace the Bahri line.

c. 1385: the Cilician plain passes to the Ramadanids as a Mamluk protectorate. 'The Mamluk Sultanate authorized Ramazan Beg's Turkmen Emirate to administer Cilicia' but 'took direct control of the towns of: Tarsus, Ayas, Sarvandikar, Sis at the four corners of Cilicia plain'; the infobox has 'Protectorate of the…

c. 1397: the Ramadanids become de facto independent. Infobox: 'Protectorate of the Mamluk Sultanate (1352-c.1397)', 'De facto independent (c. 1397-1517)'; the body: 'a protectorate of the Mamluk Sultanate until the end of the 14th century'. The year is the page's 'c.'.
1433: the Aq Qoyunlu recognise Mamluk suzerainty.
1471: the Dulkadirids are brought under the Mamluks.
1485: the Ottoman-Mamluk war opens in Cilicia.
1516: the Mamluks take Yemen from the Tahirids.
1516: the Ottomans take Syria at Marj Dabiq.
1517: the Ottomans take Cairo and the Mamluk sultanate ends.

wars.name: Mongol invasions of the Levant (Mamluk-Ilkhanid wars)
wars.outcome: Ain Jalut (September 1260) gave the Mamluks Damascus; the Mongols were beaten back to the Euphrates at Homs (October 1281); they held Syria in technical control in December 1299-January 1300; repulsed at Marj al-Suffar (1303) and in 1313; peace in 1322.

wars.name: Mamluk conquest of the Crusader states
wars.outcome: Arsuf 1265, Safed 1266, Jaffa and Antioch 1268, Krak des Chevaliers 1271, Tripoli 1289, Acre 18 May 1291: 'Mamluk rule consequently extended across all of Syria'.

wars.name: Mamluk-Makurian wars
wars.outcome: 1265 raid to Dongola; the battle of Dongola in 1276 made Makuria a Mamluk vassal and gave Lower Nubia; Mamluk expeditions of the late 1280s, 1316-17 (Abdallah Barshanbu installed, killed), 1323, and 1365-66 ('the Mamluks returned to Egypt right after, in…

wars.name: Mamluk-Armenian Cilician wars
wars.outcome: Raids in 1266 (Sis sacked), 1275 (Tarsus taken, 'the royal palace ... burned'), 1281, 1285 (tribute), 1292 (Hromkla sacked), 1299-1300, 1343-44; Sis fell on 13 April 1375 and the kingdom ended.

wars.name: Timur's invasion of Syria
wars.outcome: Timur sacked Aleppo and Damascus and 'ended his occupation of Syria in 1402'.

wars.name: Mamluk campaigns against Cyprus
wars.outcome: Barsbay's campaigns of 1425-26 captured King Janus and made Cyprus a tributary state; the tribute passed to Venice in 1489.

wars.name: Mamluk-Aq Qoyunlu conflict
wars.outcome: The Mamluks sacked Edessa (1429) and attacked Amid (1433), after which the Aq Qoyunlu recognised Mamluk suzerainty; Uzun Hasan's 1472 raid on Aleppo was routed.

wars.name: Ottoman-Mamluk War (1485-1491)
wars.outcome: Ottoman fortresses taken in Cilicia in 1485 were lost again at Adana (9 February and 15 March 1486); the Mamluks won at Agacayiri (26 August 1488), took Adana after a three-month siege and lifted the Kayseri siege in 1490; peace in May 1491 with the border at…

wars.name: Mamluk conquest of Tahirid Yemen
wars.outcome: Husain al-Kurdi's second fleet (1515) set up a tributary regime in Zabid; the whole Tahirid realm fell except Aden; the sultan was beheaded near Sanaa on 15 May.

wars.name: Ottoman-Mamluk War (1516-1517)
wars.outcome: Marj Dabiq (24 August 1516) gave Syria to Selim I; Yaunis Khan (28 October 1516) and Ridaniya (22/24 January 1517) gave him Egypt; the Hejaz followed.

certainty.note: No survey lines: the Syrian, Euphrates, Nubian and Arabian frontiers are approximate.
